newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.5/9.0 percent on Tuesday morning on sustained ample liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
They said the liquidity came from early central bank injection of some 1.055 trillion rupiah into the market.
One local bank dealer said offering of central bank overnight papers (SBIs) at eight percent limited the rate from further declines.

The central bank also offered seven-day SBIs at 11.75 percent, 14-day at 12.0 percent, one-month at 11.75 percent, three-month at 13.75 percent, six-month at 14.0 percent and 12-month at 14.5 percent.

Dealers said longer-term rates tended to ease following ample supply and overall perceptions that interest rates might ease after Bank Negara Indonesia on Monday lowered its deposit rates by 50 basis points.
They said other banks might follow suit in the near future.
One-month money edged down to 12.5 percent from 12.875 and three-month money was offered at 14.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 10.13 percent, compared with 9.63 percent on Friday.
